record.title: RoboTalk trains compact vision-language models for explicit multi-robot coordination in simulation
record.summary: The revised preprint reports 7,950 FSM-validated synthetic trajectories for 53 RoboCasa-derived kitchen tasks. In closed-loop simulation, Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct reaches 65% success on 10 held-out tasks; adding rationale targets to the Thinking model reports up to 77%. These are author-reported simulator results, not physical-robot tests.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report constructing 7,950 finite-state-machine-validated synthetic trajectories across 53 RoboCasa-derived kitchen tasks.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: With 150 trajectories per task, Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct reports 94% success on 43 training tasks and 65% on 10 held-out tasks over 10 episodes per task.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report up to 77% success on the 10 held-out simulator tasks for Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking trained with rationale targets at 120 trajectories per task.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent execution or reproduction of the simulator results was conducted.
Transfer from synthetic closed-loop simulation to physical robots and less scripted environments is untested.

brief.importance_rationale: If reproduced beyond the paper’s simulator, compact VLMs that coordinate through explicit protocols could change design choices for multi-robot task planning. The consequence is notable within constrained collaborative robotics, while real-world transfer and independent validation are unknown.
limitations: No physical robot or real-world environment was evaluated.
The held-out set contains 10 tasks with 10 episodes per task; reported success uses an FSM goal verifier.
Held-out success is not monotonic in training-set size.
Results are paper-reported; this review did not execute the public code or reproduce the results.
brief.summary: The revised preprint reports 7,950 FSM-validated synthetic trajectories for 53 RoboCasa-derived kitchen tasks. In closed-loop simulation, Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct reaches 65% success on 10 held-out tasks; adding rationale targets to the Thinking model reports up to 77%. These are author-reported simulator results, not physical-robot tests.

technical.claimed_result: In the paper’s fixed RoboCasa-derived closed-loop simulator, the reported best Instruct and rationale-trained Thinking results are 65% and 77% success on 10 held-out tasks, respectively.
technical.mechanism: Agents exchange explicit wait and release messages; a protocol enforces synchronization and exclusive workspace use. Models are fine-tuned on multimodal synthetic demonstrations, with a rationale-supervised variant for the Thinking model.
technical.regime: Closed-loop simulation of 53 kitchen tasks derived from RoboCasa; 43 training and 10 held-out tasks, 10 episodes per task; Qwen3-VL-8B models with LoRA fine-tuning.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper compares communication protocols and training variants; these are within-paper simulator comparisons and have not been independently reproduced.

brief.title: RoboTalk trains compact vision-language models for explicit multi-robot coordination in simulation
brief.why_it_matters: If the reported results hold in broader settings, structured wait-release communication and exclusive-workspace rules paired with multimodal demonstrations may improve compact VLM coordination in constrained multi-robot tasks. Transfer to real robots and less scripted environments remains unshown.
